correctness.rationale: Expanding \(B_\rho(z)=((z-s)/(1-sz))^2\), \(s=\sqrt\rho\), gives \(c_n=s^{n-2}(1-\rho)[n(1-\rho)-(1+\rho)]\). For \(0<\rho\le1/3\), only \(c_1\) is negative, so the majorant equals the ordinary value with the linear coefficient reflected. The displayed rational defect has positive denominator on \(0<r<1\), reducing the comparison to the cubic \(Q_s\). Its endpoint signs and the negativity of its convex derivative at both endpoints imply strict decrease and a unique root in \((1/3,1)\). Independent high-precision evaluation of the \(\rho=1/3\) exact cubic gave the unique in-interval root \(0.727436801449823845\ldots\), matching the record. Brevig's corollary supplies the lower bound \(R_*(\rho)\ge1/3\).
residual_risks: The construction gives an upper obstruction, not proof that the squared automorphism is globally extremal.

final_claim: For \(0<\rho\le1/3\), the squared disk automorphism \(B_\rho(z)=((z-\sqrt\rho)/(1-\sqrt\rho\,z))^2\) gives an explicit cubic upper obstruction \(R_*(\rho)\le R_2(\rho)\), where \(R_2(\rho)\) is the unique zero in \((1/3,1)\) of the stated cubic \(Q_{\sqrt\rho}\); in particular \(R_*(1/3)\le0.727436801449824\ldots\).
limitations: The upper curve is not claimed sharp and only covers \(0<\rho\le1/3\).
